Done — the Discover screen now has proper NSFW controls. Pushed as commit `02d0a3d`.

**What's new**
- An **Adult content** filter with three states: **Hide adult** (default), **Include adult** (both), and **Only adult** (18+ only). It's available in the desktop filter row, the mobile filter sheet, the active-filter chips and the shareable URL (`?adult=include` / `?adult=only`).
- **Hentai** is now in the genre list. Since AniList marks it 18+, choosing it while adult titles are hidden automatically switches the filter to "Only adult" instead of returning an empty page.
- A one-tap **18+** discovery pill, plus new genre pills for **Horror, Mecha, Mystery and Slice of Life**.
- Existing behaviour is unchanged everywhere else: any search that doesn't set the filter (home dashboard, seasonal rows, library hydration) still excludes adult titles, because the default maps to `isAdult: false`.

**One provider quirk worth knowing:** AniList returns *zero* results if `isAdult` is sent as an explicit `null`, and GraphQL can't conditionally drop an argument through a variable. So "include adult" uses a second query document with no `isAdult` argument at all, while the default document keeps it as a variable for hide/only ([queries.ts](services/anilist/queries.ts), [client.ts](services/anilist/client.ts)). Hiding remains the default.

**Verification**
- `npm run typecheck` passes; ESLint is clean on all changed files.
- 64 tests pass across validation, AniList client and outage resilience, including a new test that the hide/only/include paths send the right arguments and documents.
- I ran both generated GraphQL documents against the live AniList API: default hides adult titles, "only" returns 18+ titles, and the include variant returns adult titles when filtered by the Hentai genre.

Not run: `next build` or a browser walkthrough. One known limitation carried over from before: during an AniList outage the Kitsu fallback search doesn't apply the adult filter, so degraded search results aren't guaranteed to be SFW.

Audit complete. I read every major screen, the data layer, API routes, Supabase policies and shared components, and ran the project checks. No files were changed.

## Ground truth
- `npm run build` succeeds; TypeScript passes; 215 tests in 18 files pass.
- `npx eslint .` fails: **9 errors, ~35 warnings** (unused imports, `as any`, unescaped apostrophes, React purity/immutability rules). Nothing gates on this yet.

## What's genuinely solid
- RLS is enabled *and forced* on both user tables, anon access revoked, and the catalogue cache is deliberately inaccessible to browser roles.
- Validation boundaries are tight (Zod on every input, Episode totals, notes limits, status transitions).
- Provider resilience is unusually good: circuit breaker, TTL + stale cache, verified Kitsu ID mapping, and tests for outage paths.
- Design tokens, reduced-motion handling and `:focus-visible` exist globally ([globals.css](app/globals.css#L300)), and dialogs use native `<dialog>`.

## Fix first

**1. Light mode is advertised but broken.** Settings offers Light Mode and three light palettes, but components hardcode dark-only colours: **259 `text-white`**, **284 `border-white`**, **38 `bg-black`** occurrences. Worst offenders are [stats-view.tsx](features/stats/stats-view.tsx) (99), [continue-watching.tsx](features/library/continue-watching.tsx) (71) and [discover-browser.tsx](features/anime/discover-browser.tsx) (65). Concretely, the Discover hero heading is `text-white` over a gradient built from `--surface`, which is `#ffffff` in light mode — the text disappears. Either finish the token migration (use `text-fg`/`border-border`, keep white only over poster art) or hide light mode until it's done. This is the single biggest visual-quality gap.

**2. Hydration mismatches from clock reads during render.** [schedule-browser.tsx:205](features/schedule/schedule-browser.tsx#L205) calls `Date.now()` inside `useMemo`, and `formatAiringRelative` defaults to `Date.now()` in render. Server HTML says "Aired 18h ago", the client computes a different value → React 19 hydration errors and the lint `react-hooks/purity` failure. Move the clock into a client-only ticking store, or render relative labels after mount with a stable placeholder.

**3. There are no error boundaries anywhere.** No `error.tsx` or `global-error.tsx` exists, so one unexpected render error replaces the app with a bare 500. Adding `app/error.tsx` and `app/(app)/error.tsx` that reuse [ErrorState](components/error-state.tsx) is cheap and high value.

**4. Privacy copy overclaims.** The login footer says your library is "encrypted and private to your account" ([login-form.tsx](features/auth/login-form.tsx)); the app does authorization via RLS, not application-level encryption. Settings states it accurately. Align the copy to "private to your account, protected by row-level security" — overclaiming is a trust risk.

## Performance and security

**5. Duplicate work on every request.** [app/(app)/layout.tsx](app/(app)/layout.tsx) calls `getViewer()` and `loadLibraryItems()`, then pages call them again: dashboard and schedule call `getViewer()` again; `/schedule` calls `loadLibraryItems()` again just to learn which titles are `watching`. Each `getViewer` is a Supabase Auth round trip. Wrap both in React `cache()` for per-request dedupe, and add a repository query for watching IDs only.

**6. The marketing page is fully dynamic.** [app/page.tsx](app/page.tsx) sets `force-dynamic`, calls `getViewer()` and fetches seasonal anime on every visit. Cache the catalogue block (`revalidate`/`unstable_cache`) and split viewer-dependent navigation from the static shell.

**7. Library loading doesn't scale.** [load-library.ts](features/library/load-library.ts) loads every entry, every episode row, then hydrates metadata in 50-ID chunks on every page under `(app)`. Fine for 50 titles, painful for 1,000. Paginate the library and hydrate only the visible page.

**8. Images are all `unoptimized`.** `next.config.ts` configures AVIF/WebP and remote patterns, but every `<Image>` passes `unoptimized`, so a phone downloads the same XL posters as a desktop grid. Measure then enable the optimizer (or a custom loader with width-specific URLs).

**9. Public search endpoint has no throttle.** [route.ts](app/api/anime/search/route.ts) is unauthenticated and every cache miss spends your shared AniList quota. Add a per-IP token bucket → 429 with `Retry-After`.

**10. No security headers.** [next.config.ts](next.config.ts) only disables `x-powered-by`. Add CSP (accounting for the inline theme script), `frame-ancestors`/`X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, and HSTS in production.

**11. Episode toggles are read-modify-write.** [repositories/library.ts](repositories/library.ts) computes progress from a fresh list and then updates, without a transaction. Two devices toggling at once can diverge progress from the episode rows. A Postgres function (or an `updated_at` compare-and-set) would make it atomic.

## UX, accessibility and polish

- **Time-zone flash:** `deviceTimeZone` starts as `"UTC"` and is replaced in an effect ([preferences-provider.tsx](components/providers/preferences-provider.tsx)), so schedule times visibly jump after hydration. Persist the zone in a cookie or render placeholders until mounted.
- **Sidebar flash:** SSR always renders expanded, then collapse is read from localStorage ([sidebar-provider.tsx](components/providers/sidebar-provider.tsx)) → the content column shifts on load. Read it in the theme bootstrap script or a cookie.
- **No account deletion / clear-library action** in Settings, only JSON/CSV export. Worth adding with a typed confirmation.
- **Discover has two filter surfaces:** the page-level Filters toggle reveals `AnimeFilters`, which on mobile shows *its own* Filters button and dialog. One surface per breakpoint would be simpler.
- **Adult filter vs fallback:** during an AniList outage the Kitsu fallback ignores the adult filter, so degraded results aren't guaranteed SFW.
- **SEO/share:** no `robots.ts`, `sitemap.ts` or OG image despite a public landing page.
- **A11y:** the timezone popover has no focus trap/`aria-modal`; login "tabs" use `role="tab"` without tabpanels or arrow-key navigation; 10px white/60 labels on posters are below comfortable contrast.
- **PWA:** the service worker caches static assets only and navigations always go to the network, so the installed app shows a browser error offline. Either add an offline fallback page or drop the installable claims.
- **Dead code/config:** Fraunces and Newsreader are loaded in [layout.tsx](app/layout.tsx) but never referenced; `metaMode` in [anime-poster-card.tsx](components/anime-poster-card.tsx) is unused; ~35 unused imports. `apiFetch` also logs full error payloads to the browser console ([http.ts](lib/http.ts)).
- **Docs drift:** [README.md](README.md) still says "next/font (Inter + Sora)" and doesn't mention the new filter capabilities.
- **Tests:** excellent unit coverage, but no DOM or end-to-end tests for the highest-risk flows — add-to-library, episode toggle, timezone picker, discover filters.

## If I were sequencing this
1. Light mode (finish tokens or hide the option) — biggest visible win.
2. Clock/timezone fix (one hook) — removes hydration errors and time jumps.
3. Error boundaries + privacy copy — cheap, trust-building.
4. `cache()` dedupe + watching-only schedule query + security headers — measurable latency and hardening.

function parseId(raw: string): number | null {
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0 ? value : null;
}

export async function generateMetadata({
  params,
}: PageProps): Promise<Metadata> {
  const { id } = await params;
  const numericId = parseId(id);
  if (!numericId) {
    return { title: "Anime not found" };
  }

  try {
    const { data: anime } = await getCatalogService().getAnimeById(numericId);
    if (!anime) {
      return { title: "Anime not found" };
    }
    const title = getDisplayTitle(anime.title, true);
    return {
      title,
      description: anime.synopsis
        ? anime.synopsis.slice(0, 180)
        : `Details, ratings and related anime for ${title}.`,
      openGraph: anime.bannerImage
        ? { images: [{ url: anime.bannerImage }] }
        : undefined,
    };
  } catch {
    return { title: "Anime details" };
  }
}

function groupRelations(relations: RelatedAnime[]) {
  const groups = new Map<string, RelatedAnime[]>();
  for (const relation of relations) {
    const label = formatRelationType(relation.relationType) ?? "Related";
    const existing = groups.get(label) ?? [];
    if (existing.length < 6) {
      existing.push(relation);
    }
    groups.set(label, existing);
  }
  return [...groups.entries()];
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"lBcTH9wbKdE","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"scripts/tmp-theme-audit.mjs","instructions":"Temporary CDP harness to audit contrast and glass across theme and design combinations.","content":"import fs from "node:fs";

const PORT = 9333;
const BASE = "http://localhost:6097";

async function openTarget() {
  const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/new?about:blank`, {
    method: "PUT",
  });
  return res.json();
}

function connect(url) {
  const ws = new WebSocket(url);
  let id = 0;
  const pending = new Map();
  const events = [];
  ws.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
    const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);
    if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {
      const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id);
      pending.delete(msg.id);
      if (msg.error) reject(new Error(msg.error.message));
      else resolve(msg.result);
    } else if (msg.method) {
      events.push(msg.method);
    }
  });
  const ready = new Promise((resolve) => ws.addEventListener("open", resolve));
  const send = (method, params = {}) =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      id += 1;
      pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
    });
  return { ready, send, events, close: () => ws.close() };
}

const AUDIT = `(() => {
  const parse = (c) => { const m = c.match(/rgba?\\(([^)]+)\\)/); if (!m) return null; const p = m[1].split(/[ ,\\/]+/).filter(Boolean).map(Number); return { r:p[0],g:p[1],b:p[2],a:p[3]===undefined?1:p[3] }; } [… 1,722 characters omitted] nd(bg.r)},${Math.round(bg.g)},${Math.round(bg.b)})` });

  return {
    theme: document.documentElement.className.includes('light') ? 'light' : 'dark',
    design: document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-design'),
    body: getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor,

})()`;

const CASES = [];

await cdp.send("Runtime.enable");

}

fs.writeFileSync(".qa/theme-audit.json", JSON.stringify(results, null, 2));
cdp.close();

  if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {
    const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id);

    if (msg.error) reject(new Error(msg.error.message));
    else resolve(msg.result);
  }
});
await new Promise((r) => ws.addEventListener("open", r));
const send = (method, params = {}) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    id += 1;
    pending.set(id, { resolve, reject });
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
  });
await send("Page.enable");
await send("Runtime.enable");
await send("Page.navigate", {

Yes — pushed. Two commits are on `origin/main`: `a848080` (the first light-mode sweep) and `112c909` (this round: glass and cinematic pages).

**The glass bug was real and mechanical.** `.liquid-glass*` declared both `backdrop-filter` and `-webkit-backdrop-filter` by hand. The CSS optimizer collapsed the pair down to only the prefixed property, so the standard property was never emitted — computed style showed `backdrop-filter: none` and non-WebKit browsers got no blur at all. Glass therefore rendered as a flat, dark translucent slab. Removing the manual prefixes lets the compiler emit both forms again; the running app now reports `blur(24px) saturate(2)`.

**Theme fixes in this round**

- Removed the dark "island" I had put around the landing and auth showcase — that was the hardcoded blackish behaviour. Every landing surface, border, label and glass panel now follows the active theme; in light mode the page is light, in dark it is still the cinematic version.
- Retuned the `--faint` and `--accent` tokens per design/appearance so tertiary copy and button labels clear contrast (editorial light and shelf dark were the worst offenders).
- Fixed the breadcrumb over light glass on anime details, nested pills inside the dark hero glass, and the invalid paragraph markup in section headers.

Landing, light and dark:

![Landing in light mode](.qa/shots/final-landing-light.jpg)

![Landing in dark mode](.qa/shots/final-landing-dark.jpg)

**Verification.** I drove headless Chrome across all 24 combinations — 2 appearances × 3 design directions × landing, login, schedule and discover — and ran a contrast sweep on each. Dark mode is now clean across all three designs; light mode's only flags are poster titles sitting on black artwork scrims, which the checker can't see. Typecheck, ESLint, all 215 tests and `next build` pass.

One gap remains: `/dashboard`, `/library`, `/settings` and `/stats` need a signed-in session, so I could only verify them through the shared tokens and the queue/hero changes from the previous commit, not visually. If a specific panel there still looks wrong, tell me which one and I'll target it.
